full_judgment:
Mr. Obaidul Hassan, ,J :- This Rule was issued upon an application filed by the petitioner under Section 5 of the Limitation Act calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the delay of 98 days in filling the First Miscellaneous Appeal against the judgment . and order dated 08.08.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 2007 under Article 27 of the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (P.O. No. VII of 1973) should not be condoned. 

 2. That the short fact of the case is that the applicants as appellants have filed the instant miscellaneous appeal before this court impugning the judgment and order dated 08.08.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 2007 under Article 27(10) of the Bangladesh Housing Building Finance Corporation order, 1973 (President Order No. VII of 1973) allowing the said miscellaneous case exparte, 

 4. Mr. Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicants submits that the Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 2007 under Article 27 of the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (President Order No. VII of 1973) was filed on 28.02.2007 but no summons was served upon these appellants-applicants and they had no knowledge about the judgment passed in this case till 21.10.2010. On that day the appellant No.2 went to the Accounts Office of the respondents No.1 bank to know about their rest outstanding dues and for the first time appellants could come to know that a case was filed against them and judgment has already been pronounced in that case against them. Thereafter, the appellant No.2 on 24.10.2010 went to the Court of District Judge, Chittagong and made a thorough search and ultimately on 26.10.2010 he came to know about the filling of the Miscellaneous Case No.43 of 2007 against them by the House Building Finance Corporation. The appellants also could come to know that the judgment and order has also been pronounced on 08.08.2010. Thereafter, the appellants on 26.10.2010 filed an application for obtaining the certified copy of the judgment and order dated 08.08.2010 and other relevant papers. The certified copy of the same was made ready for delivery on 31.10.2010 and he took the delivery of the same on the same date. Thereafter he came to Dhaka on 03.11.2010 to have a consultation with his learned Advocate regarding the matter but he forgot to obtain the certified copies of the dispositions of P.Ws. and D.Ws. As per advice of their learned Advocate the appellant No.2 again went to Chittagong on 06.11.2010 and thereafter on 07.11.2010 r filed an application for obtaining the certified copies of the depositions of P.Ws. and D.Ws. and ultimately obtained the certified copies of the same on 07.11.2010. Thereafter the appellant No. l executed a power of attorney in favour of her son Tofzal Ali to file the instant miscellaneous appeal and after taking preparation and arranging money the appellant No.2 again came to Dhaka on 11.11.2010 and handed over the papers to his Advocate on 12.11.2010. Thereafter the learned Advocate after preparing the appeal filed the same to this Court on 15.11.2010. In this way a delay of 98 days has been occurred in filling this appeal which was unintentional and bonafide mistake on the part of the appellants. 

 5. Mr. Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan further submits that there is no intentional latches on the part of appellants-applicants, who were very much interested to file the miscellaneous appeal in time but the incident causing this delay was beyond their control as the present applicants were prevented by sufficient cause in filling the instant miscellaneous appeal within time. He further submits that the applicants regret for the said unintentional latches and bonafide delay and crave indulgence of this Court to condone the delay cause in filing the miscellaneous appeal otherwise the applicants shall be highly prejudiced and shall suffer an irreparable loss and injury. 

 13. Section 28 and Section 46 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 specially prohibited the application of Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 in Artha Rin Cases. 

 14. From the above discussions we find that in the BHBFC Order, 1973 there is no overriding clause but in other special enactments there are overriding clauses. Thus in the enactments where over riding clauses are there and specific provisions prohibiting the applicability of the Limitation Act is mentioned, the applications made under the provision of Limitation Act are not maintainable. On the other hand in the cases under the BHBFC Order, 1973 the applicability of the provision of Limitation Act has not been made prohibited as well as there in no any overriding clause in the said Act, further more applicability of the Code of Civil Procedure is available in disposing of the cases under the BHBFC Order, 1973 thus there is a clear distinction between BHBFC Order, 1973 and other special enactments as mentioned above. 

 17. The explanation for delay in filing the instant miscellaneous appeal as explained in paragraph No.2 of the application appears to us satisfactory. There was no intentional latches on the part of the appellants and further more since the appellants regretted for the unintentional latches, we consider it as bonafide delay. Thus we are inclined to condone the delay in filing the instant miscellaneous appeal. 

 18. Accordingly the Rule is made absolute. The delay of 98 days in filing the miscellaneous appeal is hereby condoned.
